newsitem.title: BOSNIA: UNHCR slams Germany for deporting Bosnians.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR slams Germany for deporting Bosnians.

text.p: The main U.N. relief agency criticised German authorities on Wednesday for forcing a group of Bosnians to return to their country without ensuring the refugees could safely return to their homes.

"I am disheartened to learn some of these people were woken up in the middle of the night and forced onto the flight back to Sarajevo," said Carrol Faubert, special envoy for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
Faubert said in a statement that refugees who fled the 1992-95 war in Bosnia should not be forced to come back until their return could be "viable and safe".

Bavarian authorities deported 44 Bosnians on Tuesday and flew them to the capital Sarajevo. Nine of the refugees had no relatives to stay with and had to sleep at a transit centre sponsored by the UNHCR.

Three of the refugees interviewed by U.N. aid workers had homes in what is now Serb-controlled territory. As Croats or Moslems, trying to return to Serb conquered territory would clearly put them at risk, the UNHCR said.

"We have repeatedly called on host governments to continue providing temporary protection to Bosnians who originate from areas to where they cannot presently return in safety," said Faubert, the UNHCR's envoy to former Yugoslavia.
Although this week's deportations took place under a bilateral agreement between Bosnia and Germany, Sarajevo officials criticised German authorities for their handling of the operation.

Bosnian refugee officials said Germany had sent back some people who had nowhere to go and accused authorities of treating the refugees like criminals, even though only a handful had any criminal record.
Germany accepted more refugees from Bosnia than any other Western European state. More than 300,000 fled to Germany following the violent disintegration of former Yugoslavia.
Nationalist authorities, in clear violation of a 1995 peace treaty, have blocked refugees from rival ethnic groups from returning to their homes in towns across the country.
The war left Bosnia divided into ethnic ghettoes and more than one million refugees fled the country.
